_help: Read by the tutor package at import (AGENTS.md Rule 0: nothing in tutor/*.py names a path, a module, a model or a limit).

paths: relative to the vault unless said otherwise. {vault}, ~ and {module_dir} are filled at runtime. inboxes.module is a folder looked for inside EVERY module folder; inboxes.shared are extra folders (outside the vault allowed) scanned as well, skipped when absent.
state: where private tutor state lives, relative to the repo (memory/ is git-ignored). DENISSE_TUTOR_STATE overrides it.
modules: how a module folder name becomes a code and a title (mirrors scripts/next_lecture.json). Modules are discovered from the vault folder names; there is no list here.

match: regexes that find a week number or a module code in a folder name, a file name, or the first content_chars of a file's text. Keep capture group 1 as the number. First hit wins, folder before file name before contents.
extract: which extensions are read how. audio is off unless audio.enabled is true (faster_whisper, installed already; no download happens here).

model: config_entry names the entry in config.json 'models' (model_config.py); context comes from brain.json limits.num_ctx, DENISSE_NUM_CTX winning, the same knob the brain uses. chars_per_token and reserve_tokens size the chunks a long lecture is cut into.

prompt: what the local model is asked, per chunk. {module} {code} {week} {sources} {part} {parts} {text} are filled. It must answer with the JSON shape in prompt.schema; a reply that isn't JSON gets one retry with prompt.retry appended. bad_escape: a backslash in the reply that is the model's LaTeX, not a JSON escape (\pi, \frac, \theta, \neq: no escape, or a letter escape followed by a lowercase letter) -- doubled before parsing; a closing brace the reply stopped short of is put back (model.parse).

note: the tutor note's name, frontmatter and section templates. {module} {code} {week} {slug} {today} {outcomes_n} ... are filled. The name slug must be unique across the vault (scripts/vault_contract.py), hence the suffix.
limits: caps on what one note holds, so a long lecture gives a usable note, not a dump.

unmatched_reasons.module: no module: no module code or module name in the folder, file name or first page
unmatched_reasons.week: no week: no 'Week N' / 'Lecture N' in the folder, file name or first page
unmatched_reasons.empty: no text could be read from it
unmatched_reasons.audio_off: audio file; audio.enabled is false in tutor/tutor.json

prompt.system: You are a careful study tutor for a university engineering module. You read lecture material and write down exactly what it teaches: nothing invented, nothing from outside the text. Equations are written in LaTeX between $ signs. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
prompt.user:
Module: {module} ({code}), Week {week}. Material: {sources}. This is part {part} of {parts}.

From the text below, list what a student must be able to do after this lecture (learning outcomes), the key methods and equations it uses, any worked examples it contains, short self-check questions, and the topics it covers with what each one assumes you already know.

Reply with JSON of exactly this shape:
{schema}

Rules: keep every item short (one line); use only what the text says; LaTeX for every equation ($...$); leave a list empty rather than guess; no markdown outside the JSON.

TEXT:
{text}
prompt.retry: Your last reply was not valid JSON. Reply again with ONLY the JSON object, no prose, no code fences.

note.name: {slug}-week-{week}-tutor
front: description: "{code} Week {week} tutor note: learning outcomes, key methods and equations, worked examples and a check-yourself list, extracted by {tutor} from the KEATS material. Regenerated when the material changes; edit a copy, not this."
generated_callout: > [!info] Written by {tutor} from the material below

> Everything here was read out of the files listed under Sources by the local model, chunk by chunk. It is a map of what the lecture teaches, not a replacement for your own write-up. If it is wrong, the material wins.
index_front: description: "{code} {module}: {tutor}'s tutor notes by week and the module's topic map. Regenerated by python -m tutor ingest."
note.index_none: - No tutor notes yet: put the KEATS files in the inbox and run `python -m tutor ingest`.

say.no_inbox: no inbox folder found (looked for '{module}' inside each module folder, and {shared})
say.no_module: no module called '{text}' in the vault; known: {modules}
say.no_topics: no topic map for {module} yet; run python -m tutor ingest
say.dry_model: dry run: nothing extracted and nothing written
say.no_repo: the vault has no .git at its root
say.sources: {module}: {n} vault note(s) to make cards from ({own} of yours)
say.cards_no_json: the model did not answer with JSON cards
say.cards_done: {module}: {n} card(s) from {sources} note(s); {made} note(s) asked, {kept} unchanged, {failed} failed
say.no_cards: no cards for {module} yet; run python -m tutor cards {module}
say.tsv: anki tsv     {path} ({n} card(s); import it in Anki: File > Import)
say.anki_down: AnkiConnect not reachable at {url} ({why}): wrote the TSV only, recorded no review stats
say.anki_off: AnkiConnect is off in tutor.json (anki.connect.enabled): wrote the TSV only, recorded no review stats
say.anki_stats: anki stats   {deck}: {cards} card(s), {reviewed} reviewed, {weak} weak topic(s)

_help_don: name: what the study tutor is called (Chuen, 5 Nov 2026). Every deck, note line and commit message takes it from here.

don: the tutor's area in the vault, where its memory and Chuen's progress live (Chuen, 5 Nov: 'add my progress and memory back into' Obsidian). folder is relative to the vault; data is the sidecar subfolder for the JSON a note can't hold (what was read, topic maps, cards, Anki stats). paths.state (memory/tutor) is the OLD place: anything found there is copied here once, and read from there while the new copy is missing.

sources: which vault notes count as a module's material, besides everything in its folder: a note whose frontmatter keys name the module (code, slug or title), or which links to one of link_names. exclude_dirs are never walked.

cards: what is asked of each source note. kinds say how many cards of each sort and which engine writes them: local = Ollama (model.config_entry), claude = delegate.py (Chuen's Claude plan through the claude CLI, never an API key). A source note is asked again only when its text changes.

anki: one deck per module (deck), one note type (note_type). tsv: the file Chuen can import by hand. connect: AnkiConnect, used when reachable; cards are matched by their Id field, so a re-sync updates, never duplicates.
weak: how review stats become a weak topic. A topic is weak when its reviewed cards average at least lapse_rate lapses, or its mean ease is under ease_below (Anki's percent). score orders them.
learner: what Don files in the learner model (learner/), as measured beliefs with evidence; never an edit to his notes.
git: every vault write is committed through scripts/vault_git.py commit_owned, only the files written, never under never_dirs.
name: Don

hub_front: description: "{tutor}, the study tutor in Denisse: what it has read, the cards it made and how Chuen's reviews are going, per module. Regenerated by python -m tutor; edit a copy, not this."

{tutor} reads the KEATS material and your notes for each module, writes tutor notes and cards, and keeps track of what Anki says you keep forgetting. Its working files are in `{data}/` beside this note.
progress_front: description: "{code} {module}: what {tutor} has read, the cards it made and the topics Anki says need work. Regenerated by python -m tutor."
don.progress_material: - {files} file(s) read from the KEATS inbox; tutor notes for week(s) {weeks}.
don.progress_anki_none: - No review stats yet: they come from AnkiConnect on `python -m tutor anki-sync`.
don.progress_anki_synced: - Last read from Anki on {date}: {cards} card(s), {reviewed} reviewed.
progress_table: | Topic | Cards | Reviewed | Lapses | Ease | Due | Weak |
don.progress_exams: - {n} exam-style question(s) marked, {mean}% on average; last: {marks}/{total} on {title} ({date}).
don.progress_practice_none: - Nothing explained or practised yet: ask {tutor} in chat.
cards_front: description: "{code} {module}: every card {tutor} made for Anki, by source note. Regenerated by python -m tutor cards; review in Anki, not here."
> Made from the notes linked under each heading. Anki deck: `{deck}`.

recall.describe: recall cards: a definition, a named result or an equation to state from memory

method.describe: method cards: given a situation, which method to use and why

problem.describe: short worked problems: a small problem on the front, the worked answer in a few steps on the back

cards.system: You are {tutor}, a careful study tutor writing Anki cards for a university engineering student. Use only what the note says; nothing invented. Equations in LaTeX between \( and \). Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.

anki.css: .card { font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 20px; text-align: left; color: black; background-color: white; } .source, .topic { font-size: 14px; color: #666; }

learner.weak_claim: Finds {topic} ({module}) hard to keep: it keeps lapsing in Anki
learner.ok_claim: Keeps {topic} ({module}) in Anki now, after it was a weak topic
learner.evidence: {tutor}, Anki review stats {date}: {lapses} lapse(s) over {reviewed} reviewed card(s), mean ease {ease}%

messages.ingest: {tutor}: tutor notes and topic maps from the KEATS inbox
messages.migrate: {tutor}: move tutor memory into the vault

_help_teach: teach (part 3): explaining a topic. The material is the topic map entry, the tutor notes of the weeks it names and his own notes that mention it (sources.py), capped to material_share of the model's chunk. learner_areas are the learner-model areas quoted to the model (how he likes to be taught). engines name cards.engines entries: local = Ollama, hard/fallback = delegate.py (Claude). hard_topics: topic words Chuen marks as hard, always Claude. self_check: what a local answer must have to stand; one that fails goes to the fallback engine in the background (BACKGROUND in chat.py), the local answer given meanwhile.

quiz: the short check from the cards (part 2). questions is the default count, also the end-of-round check study mode offers (study_mode.set_round_end). order: which cards first -- weak and due come from the Anki stats. mark_engine marks his answers against the card backs.

exam: longer problems in the style of the coursework and past papers found in the module folder (paper_globs, relative to it; PDFs and Office files read by extract.py). engine writes the question and a mark scheme; marking_engine marks his answer against it, step by step. The open question and the history live in practice_file.

chat: every sentence the chat tools (tutor/chat.py, registered in tools.py) return to the model. intro is the first sentence of every result, so a reply that leaves the tutor out still gets it (tool_policy.json reply_must_mention). In quiz and exam, what follows ' Tell him' is for the model only: brain.json honesty.result_cut_markers cuts it off when the result itself is shown (must_mention_replaces), so he sees the questions and not the instructions. {tutor} is the name above.

teach.learner_none: - nothing known yet; teach plainly, one step at a time
teach.system: You are {tutor}, a patient study tutor for a university engineering student. Teach from the material given: his lecture notes and his own notes. Say when the material does not cover something rather than inventing it. Equations in LaTeX between $ signs. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
teach.schema: {"summary": "one line: what the topic is for", "steps": ["..."], "question": "...", "answer": "...", "confident": true}
lessons_front: description: "{code} {module}: every topic {tutor} explained in chat, step by step, with the check question. Regenerated by the tutor tools; edit a copy, not this."
> Each lesson was taught from the notes linked under it ({tutor}'s tutor notes and your own). Newest first.
teach.lessons_none: - Nothing explained yet: ask {tutor} to explain a topic in chat.

quiz.mark_system: You are {tutor}, marking a student's short answers against the answers on his revision cards. Be fair: the same idea in other words is right; a missing key part is wrong. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
quiz.offer: Round {round} done: {tutor} can give a {n}-question check on what he has been studying -- offer it, and quiz him if he says yes.

exam.system: You are {tutor}, setting an exam-style problem for a university engineering student, in the style of his module's coursework and past papers. Use only the material given for the content. Equations in LaTeX between $ signs. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
exam.style_none: (no coursework or past paper found: set a standard multi-part problem)
exam.schema: {"title": "a few words", "question": "the full problem, parts labelled (a), (b)...", "marks": 20, "mark_scheme": [{"step": "what earns the marks", "marks": 4}]}
exam.mark_system: You are {tutor}, marking a university engineering student's answer to an exam-style problem against its mark scheme. Mark each step of the scheme: say what he earned and why, in a sentence he can act on. Be strict on method, lenient on arithmetic slips that carry through. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
exam.mark_schema: {"marks": 12, "total": 20, "steps": [{"step": "...", "awarded": 2, "of": 4, "comment": "..."}], "feedback": "two or three sentences: what to revise"}
note_front: description: "{code} {module}: the exam-style questions {tutor} set in chat, Chuen's marks and the feedback, and his quiz scores. Regenerated by the tutor tools; edit a copy, not this."
exam.entry_open_line: Answer it in chat and {tutor} will mark it.
exam.none: - Nothing yet: ask {tutor} for an exam question in chat.

chat.no_modules: {intro} There are no module folders in the vault yet, so nothing to teach from.
chat.no_module: {intro} I don't know a module called '{text}'. The modules in the vault are: {modules}.
chat.which_module: {intro} Which module is that for: {modules}? Ask him in one short question, then call again with the module.
chat.no_material: {intro} There's nothing in the vault about '{topic}' for {module} yet -- no tutor note or note of his names it. Say so plainly; offer to explain it from general knowledge only if he asks.
chat.from_claude: explained by Claude from the lecture notes
chat.escalated: {intro} {why} so {tutor} has asked Claude for a proper explanation of {topic} ({module}); it will pop up here when it's done and go into {note}. Tell him that.
chat.why_hard: {topic} is marked as a hard topic,
chat.why_check: the local model's explanation didn't pass {tutor}'s own check,
chat.why_dry: {topic} needs Claude, but hand-offs are off in this run,
chat.no_cards: {intro} No cards for {module} yet, so nothing to quiz from. Make them with: python -m tutor cards {module}
chat.no_stats: {intro} No Anki review stats for {module} yet, so nothing is measured as weak. He needs to review the cards in Anki and run: python -m tutor anki-sync
chat.weak: {intro} Weak in {module} by his Anki reviews (synced {date}): {topics}.{learner}
chat.weak_none: {intro} Nothing measured as weak in {module}: {cards} card(s), {reviewed} reviewed, no topic lapsing (synced {date}).{learner}
chat.exam_style_none: the lecture notes (no coursework or past paper in the module folder)
chat.no_open: {intro} There's no open question for {module} to mark. Give him an exam question or a quiz first.
chat.marking: {intro} {tutor} has sent his answer to Claude for marking against the mark scheme; the marks and step-by-step feedback will pop up here and go into {note}. Tell him that.
chat.mark_failed: {intro} Couldn't mark that: {why}. His answer is kept; try again later.
chat.model_failed: {intro} The model didn't give a usable {what}: {why}. Say so; don't make one up.
